Then under each of the six mutants: all six exit 0, 709 pass, identical test COUNT across all seven runs, which is how the agent knows no file was silently dropped under load. m-fold: the example mission with code/src/core/domain/ϴguard.ts on disk (U+03F4 GREEK CAPITAL THETA SYMBOL) cited as ϑguard.ts (U+03D1 GREEK THETA SYMBOL). Both names created from Node, never through shell argv, so no Unicode round-trip. Verified on the volume first: reading ϑguard.ts opens the on-disk ϴguard.ts, so the pointer resolves here and would not on a case-sensitive runner. Pristine: exit 1, gaps, conformance 1. One mission exercising all three functions at once.

m-fold-theta, the control that proves m-fold is not an accident: same on-disk U+03F4 name, pointer written with U+03B8 (ordinary theta). Under the caseFold mutant it STILL refuses, byte-identical, because plain toLowerCase() collapses U+03F4 onto U+03B8 and the realpath rung re-derives the verdict. It is the U+03D1 spelling that gets past both rungs. Choosing the wrong control here is precisely how one concludes harmless for a live false green.

REACHABILITY INSTRUMENTATION, three modes patched into dist and run over the whole corpus (723 unit tests, the four missions, the battery): one records every evaluation of the else arm, one records every argument isSpelling receives, one records the truthiness of the roots tuple each caller passes. Each restores the pristine build and re-checks its sha256.

verdicts.evidence: Survives on macOS too, so not a filesystem artifact: net exit 0 / fail 0 over 723 tests, the four extra nets exit 0 with byte-identical output, self-gate and all four missions byte-identical on json, clear text and sarif. The mutated arm is NOT dead at the gate — the roots instrumentation logged 59 calls, 20 of them arriving with a truthy first root and a null second, so the literal IS substituted on every one of them and the payload still does not move, because the first accepted root is still the project root and no real spelling starts with the literal. It moves the moment the FIRST root is falsy, a shape the exported signature accepts: 3 of 196 battery cases moved, each turning a correct relative path into a climbing path that resolves nowhere. A consumer acts on that directly — it is the string the gate tells an operator to paste. Battery sensitivity is not in doubt: the same 196 cases moved for three other mutants and for a deliberate control.
verdicts.mission: battery P11/P12/P15; reachability mode 'roots' for the gate-side observation

verdicts.evidence: Net exit 0 / fail 0, four extra nets exit 0, every mission byte-identical. Direct drive: 2 of 196 moved, both turning null into the bare parent marker. With the guard defeated the gate would render 'The file is spelled ..' — a directory prescribed as the file to cite, the RWD-2026-0034 family of remedy-that-does-not-work. Unreachable through the gate on any platform because the relative form equals the parent marker only when the spelling IS the parent of the canonical project root, and the pointer layer has already refused anything that is not a regular file. Not equivalent: the same battery that stays flat for the dead arm moves twice here.

Measured separately from its neighbour on the same line — the two are only distinguishable by column. Net exit 0 / fail 0, every mission byte-identical, the same 2 of 196 battery cases moving with the same values. Mechanically it is the stronger of the two: rewriting the literal makes the disjunct a test the preceding truthiness check already covers, so the refusal is deleted outright rather than merely bypassed. Same unreachability, same absence of any net.

verdicts.evidence: The disjunct is subsumed by the conjunction beside it: for r === "", "" !== ".." is true, "".startsWith("../") is false and isAbsolute("") is false — on path.posix and path.win32 alike — so the second operand already returns true and under is unchanged. SENSITIVITY CONTROL: making the first disjunct decisive would need relative() to return "" while "" === ".." or isAbsolute("") held; no platform Node supports does that. Verified: projectRelativeSpelling("/w/repo", "/w/repo") is null under both (the empty rel is refused two lines later by !rel), and eight probe scenarios plus 11 conformance cases are identical.

verdicts.evidence: Lets under accept a spelling that is the PARENT of an accepted root. Shielded upstream: projectRelativeSpelling is only ever called on r.spelling, and resolvePointer produces a spelling only for a path already admitted by real === baseAbs || real.startsWith(baseAbs + sep) or real === repo || real.startsWith(repo + sep), which evidenceReport then reads only after isRegularFile(abs). So the argument is always a FILE at or under an accepted root, never a strict ancestor, and relative(root, spelling) can never be ".."; the near shape is shielded again by if (!rel || rel === ".." || isAbsolute(rel)) return null. STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a DIRECT call does separate them — projectRelativeSpelling("/w", "/w/repo/proj", "/w/repo") is "../.." under the mutant and null on the shipped build — so one line in evidence-spelling-ladder.test.js retires this row without waiting for a mission that can reach it.
